identity_held_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Job Description:
The Senior Manager of Quality is responsible for establishing and leading all quality activities for a complex aerospace development program from prototype through production readiness. This role serves as the primary quality leader embedded within the program team and partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Flight Test, and Program Management to ensure products are designed, developed, tested, and transitioned to production with quality, reliability, and mission success as foundational objectives.
The Senior Manager of Quality will build and lead a multidisciplinary quality team while implementing scalable quality systems, risk management processes, problem-solving disciplines, and development quality practices appropriate for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense technology organization.
This position requires balancing speed of development with disciplined engineering rigor to support aggressive program schedules while ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and company requirements.

What you'll do:
Development Quality Leadership
Serve as the quality leader for XBAT development.
Establish quality strategy, objectives, and metrics aligned with program milestones.
Integrate quality requirements into the product development lifecycle.
Ensure quality considerations are incorporated during system architecture, design reviews, verification, validation, and qualification activities.
Partner with Engineering leadership to identify and mitigate technical and programmatic risks.
Drive a culture of proactive quality and continuous improvement throughout the program.
Design & Configuration Quality
Ensure quality requirements are appropriately captured in product definitions, specifications, and design documentation.
Participate in design reviews, change control boards, and configuration management activities.
Ensure full configuration and traceability for all material installed into prototype aircraft.
Evaluate engineering changes for quality and production readiness impacts.
Support requirements verification and validation planning.
Drive design-for-manufacturing, design-for-quality, and design-for-reliability initiatives.
Risk Management & Reliability
Lead quality participation in program risk management activities.
Establish and maintain FRACAS processes for development and flight test phases of the program.
Facilitate root cause and corrective action investigations for design, manufacturing, supplier, and field failures.
Support reliability growth planning and execution.
Monitor defect trends, failure modes, and reliability metrics to identify systemic risks.
Verification, Validation & Test Quality
Develop quality oversight strategies for laboratory, ground, and flight test activities.
Ensure test results, anomalies, and nonconformances are appropriately documented and dispositioned.
Support qualification and certification efforts.
Establish processes for managing test escapes, failures, and corrective actions.
Nonconformance & Corrective Action Management
Lead Material Review Board activities for development hardware.
Establish scalable processes for nonconformance management.
Drive root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methodologies.
Ensure timely and effective corrective and preventive actions.
Track effectiveness of corrective actions through closure.
Production Readiness & Industrialization
Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams to transition products from prototype to production.
Define quality requirements for production readiness reviews.
Support development of inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and control strategies.
Ensure lessons learned from development are incorporated into production processes.
Lead quality planning activities supporting low-rate initial production and rate increases.
Quality Management System
Develop and implement quality processes supporting aerospace development programs.
Ensure compliance with AS9100, customer requirements, and internal procedures.
Drive continuous improvement of development quality processes.
Support internal and external audits as required.
Establish scalable systems that support future production growth.
Leadership & Team Development
Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing quality organization.
Recruit and develop quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians.
Establish clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.
Promote a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and collaboration.
Develop organizational capabilities to support future company growth.
Required qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Aerospace Engineering, or related technical discipline.
10+ years of experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, space, or other highly regulated industries.
5+ years of leadership experience managing technical quality organizations.
Experience supporting complex product development programs from concept through production transition.
Strong knowledge of quality systems, engineering development processes, and aerospace manufacturing.
Experience leading root cause investigations and corrective action programs.
Experience with risk management, reliability engineering, and failure analysis.
Working knowledge of AS9100 quality management systems.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.
Preferred qualifications:
Experience supporting UAV, aerospace, defense, aviation, autonomous systems, or advanced technology programs.
Experience leading quality organizations during rapid company growth.
Background in systems engineering, reliability engineering, or development engineering.
Experience with flight test programs and qualification testing.
ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or equivalent certification.
Familiarity with government defense programs and customer quality requirements.

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Supplier Quality (R6220)
identity_held_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

What you'll do:
Develop the supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, surveillance, performance management, and corrective-action activities across Shield AI’s global aerospace and defense supply base.
Establish supplier-quality priorities, allocate resources, and translate functional objectives into staffing, workload, and execution plans that support product, program, and organizational needs.
Develop Supplier Quality leaders and engineering personnel through coaching, performance management, succession planning, workforce development, and technical mentorship.
Oversee supplier qualification, risk assessments, periodic performance reviews, supplier audits, source inspections, and approved-supplier status across complex aerospace hardware, commodities, and manufacturing processes.
Ensure supplier requirements are effectively flowed down and that suppliers comply with applicable quality management system, engineering, customer, contractual, regulatory, and statutory requirements.
Escalate significant supplier-quality risks and direct SCARs, supplier recovery efforts, and capability-improvement plans that could affect product quality, delivery, mission readiness, or program execution.
Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program teams to address supplier producibility, design-for-manufacturability, process capability, technical execution, and quality risks.
Advance supplier-quality processes, business systems, data analytics, and continuous-improvement practices that strengthen supplier capability, product quality, delivery performance, and supply-base resilience.
Required qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or another related technical discipline.
At least 7 years of relevant experience, including 2–5 years of leadership or people-management experience with direct responsibility for Quality Engineering and/or Supplier Quality Engineering personnel.
Strong working knowledge of AS9100 and/or ISO 9001 quality-management systems, as well as aerospace and defense supplier-quality requirements.
Demonstrated proficiency in root-cause analysis and structured problem-solving methods, including 8D, 5 Whys, and fishbone analysis.
Experience with supplier qualification, supplier development, PPAP, and First Article Inspection processes, including AS9102 requirements.
Understanding of ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and other requirements applicable to aerospace and defense suppliers.
Demonstrated people-leadership capability, including coaching, performance management, organizational development, and building high-performing technical teams.
Strong cross-functional collaboration, executive communication, and supplier relationship-management skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems.
Ability to travel to Shield AI manufacturing locations and supplier sites domestically and, as needed, internationally—up to approximately 20% of the time.
Preferred qualifications:
ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Manager (CQM), or equivalent quality certification.
Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
Experience leading supplier-quality functions in a high-growth aerospace, defense, autonomy, robotics, or advanced-manufacturing environment.
Experience supporting the production and qualification of complex electromechanical, electronic, precision-machined, composite, or avionics hardware.
Full-time regular employee offer package:
Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity
 
Temporary employee offer package:
Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)
 
Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager – Manufacturing Engineering & Technology
identity_held_roles.description:
Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 We are seeking a dynamic Senior Manager of Manufacturing Engineering and Technology to oversee our aerospace component production processes. This pivotal role will lead teams in achieving operational excellence while collaborating with cross-functional departments to continuously enhance manufacturing operations. The ideal candidate will be results-driven, adept at resource management, and committed to maintaining high-quality standards in a fast-paced environment.
 
 We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
 
 Position Specific Details: 
 Location: Space Coast, FL
 Relocation: Available
 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Lead and optimize manufacturing operations to ensure efficiency and quality.
 Develop and execute production plans to meet delivery schedules.
 Mentor manufacturing teams, providing guidance and fostering a positive work environment, encouraging teamwork and openness, and sharing information to foster unity.
 Collaborate with engineering, quality, and supply chain teams to address manufacturing challenges, balancing day-to-day activities with strategic planning.
 Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance production processes and metrics.
 Monitor production performance and provide regular updates to senior management, demonstrating sound judgment and understanding the impact of team actions on business drivers and adapting to industry changes.
 Ensure compliance with safety, regulatory, and company standards, and take initiative on opportunities and challenges with urgency and enthusiasm.
 Manage budget and resource allocation for manufacturing activities.
 Support new product introductions and scale up production capabilities.
 Evaluate inputs and criteria to make informed decisions with a focus on decision quality.
 
 Team Focus & Domain Expertise: 
 In this role you will lead and mentor a team of Manufacturing Engineers and Planners who are developing and supporting the design and fabrication of machined parts, advanced metal forming, and wire harnesses. This role will require you to demonstrate your ability to interact with the vehicle to proactively improve design for manufacturability, eliminate barriers and solve unforeseen technical problems.
 
 Minimum Qualifications: 
 5+ years of experience managing a team within a manufacturing or aerospace environment.
 5+ years of experience as an individual contributor within a manufacturing or aerospace environment.
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, aerospace, Military, or equivalent experience required.
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with teams and stakeholders.
 Ability to analyze data and metrics to drive decision-making and operational improvements.
 Ability to lift 50lbs and comfortable working at heights (work stands, ladders, lifts) and/or in confined spaces. 
 Proficiency in digital tools, including Windows and Microsoft Office applications. 
 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Industry certification, trade school training and/or degree in related field.  
 Experience in aerospace manufacturing, integration, or other relevant field
 Experience working on fluid systems with applied chemistry fundamentals.
 Experience with advanced manufacturing technologies and tools (e.g., CAD software, ERP systems).
 Ability to adapt to changing priorities and handle multiple tasks simultaneously.
 Familiarity with regulatory compliance in aerospace manufacturing.
 Proven track record of successful team leadership and project management.
 Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing principles and practices.
 Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma certification.  
 Willingness to work overtime.  
 Culture Statement 
 Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Export Control Regulations 
 Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 Background Check 
 Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
 Required for Certain Job Profiles:  Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
 Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
 Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
 
 Benefits 
 Benefits include:  Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
 Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
 Paid Time Off:  Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
 Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here .

 Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation 
 Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at  EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE:

The Senior Manager, Quality owns program quality end to end and leads the Quality Engineering team that supports it. You will build and lead a team of Quality Engineers across the program's process areas, owning requirements into our AS9100D quality management system, and be the single point of accountability for whether product is built to spec, on schedule, and with the objective quality evidence to prove it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Team leadership — build, lead, and develop the Quality Engineering team supporting the project across sheet metal, welding and forming, NDT, foundry and forging, machining, and additive manufacturing.

• Staffing and coverage — close the open QE positions on the program, set priorities, and ensure every process area has quality coverage.

• Development and standards — coach QEs, set consistent standards of practice, and grow special-process competency (welding, NDT) across the team.

• Cross-functional partnership — represent quality with Build Engineering, Operations, and the program team, and serve as the escalation point for quality decisions on Nautilus.

• Program quality for Nautilus — first-article inspection (AS9102), product qualification, and quality across the build from receipt to delivery.

• Non-conformance and corrective action — control non-conforming material and customer escapes, drive root-cause and corrective action to closure, and own escape management for the program.

• Supplier and receiving quality — flow requirements to suppliers, verify certifications and OQE at receipt, and build receiving capability for controlled material.

• Audit readiness — prepare for and lead customer, and AS9100 audits for the program, and own the internal-audit posture that keeps it compliant.

• Metrics and reporting — quality KPIs, escape trends, and program quality status to leadership.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

• 8+ years in quality within defense, marine, nuclear, or aerospace manufacturing, including direct people-management of a quality team.

• Proven command of AS9100 / ISO 9001 and hands-on experience integrating customer and regulatory requirements into a QMS.

• Track record building quality processes and teams in a fast-scaling or startup manufacturing environment.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance; U.S. person under ITAR.



What Will Set You Apart

• Background at a submarine prime or shipyard (e.g., General Dynamics Electric Boat, HII Newport News) or a qualified SUBSAFE supplier.

• Knowledge of NAVSEA and SUBSAFE / Material Level I requirements (objective quality evidence, controlled material, traceability, cleanliness).

• AS9100 / ISO 9001 lead-auditor certification; familiarity with welding and NDT special-process controls (Nadcap).

• CQE, CMQ/OE, or equivalent quality certification.

• Experience standing up program quality from the ground up — writing the system, not just running it.




BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
 401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

identity_held_roles.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.



Commissioning Chief Engineer, Marauder

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing defense autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Summary:

In this role you will be responsible for the commissioning and operation of the engine room and all associated machinery aboard a novel autonomous vessel. You will ensure that all marine systems — including but not limited to main propulsion, auxiliary machinery, fuel oil, lubrication, cooling, and associated environmental equipment — are properly tested and validated through structured commissioning processes and integrated with the vessel's autonomy and software control systems to support reliable manned, remote, and autonomous operation.

The ideal candidate will possess strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities, along with the ability to develop procedures and processes in support of a novel commissioning environment. Have a strong grasp on vessel engineering systems with the ability to work independently on issues, including drafting and refining operational and technical documentation where none previously existed. A steadfast commitment to safety and adherence to maritime regulations is essential for ensuring the highest standards in vessel operations.

Responsibilities

 - Lead and support commissioning activities for autonomous vessels, including system testing, validation, and troubleshooting prior to and during operation.

 - Collaborate with autonomy and software engineering teams to verify integration between traditional machinery control systems and the vessel's autonomy stack across manned, remote, and autonomous operating modes

 - Develop, write, and refine standard operating procedures, checklists, and technical documentation from scratch in the absence of established processes

 - Complete all necessary maintenance on vessel machinery.

 - Always be on-call while on-hitch to address any issues that arise.

 - Manage inventory and ordering of spare parts.

 - Assist in the shipboard execution of mission objectives.

 - Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with team members, stakeholders, and senior management.

 - Problem-solving abilities and a proactive approach to addressing challenges.

 - Strong leadership skills to lead a team in a dynamic environment and pitch in when your skills are applicable while working across teams.

 - Travel to multiple locations while on hitch

Required Qualifications

 - Valid U.S. Coast Guard MMC

 - National Chief Engineer of Motor, Unlimited Horsepower Endorsement.

 - STCW Endorsements of Chief Engineer, OICEW, Basic Training, Advanced Firefighting

 - Valid USCG STCW Medical Certificate

 - Valid TWIC, USCG STCW Medical Certificate, and Passport.

 - Proficiency in maritime engineering systems, particularly electrical systems

 - Ability to work both independently and as a part of a group

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams

 - Pass background check and USCG/DOT drug testing prior to onboarding.

 - Security clearance and eligibility required

 - Projected 28/28 schedule

Desired Qualifications

 - Familiar with jet-drive marine engines

 - Experience with autonomous or unmanned systems

 - Experience with software engineering

 - Experience with automation systems.

Physical Demands

 - Ability to certify as “fit for work” by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water

 - Frequently and repetitively, lift, push and carry up to 50 lbs.

 - Will be exposed to marine environments, including sun, wind, rain, cold, and saltwater spray, often for extended periods

 - Must be able to operate in daylight, low-light, and night conditions using marine navigation systems and visual cues

 - Ability to perform physically demanding work i.e. stoop, lay, bend, reach, squat, kneel, crouch, twist and crawl for extended periods of time including up to 12 hours/day

 - Climb and maintain balance on ladders, platforms, or other high structures

 - Ability to stand and walk for up to 10 hours a day, including over varied and uneven terrain

 - Climb and maintain balance on ladders, scaffolding or other high structures

identity_held_roles.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




POSITION OVERVIEW

The Staff Quality Engineer serves as the VP of Quality's senior technical quality expert responsible for driving multi-site RCCA culture, supporting engineering and manufacturing quality. Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, this role leads enterprise-wide technical investigations, drives engineering-based Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), and partners across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Product, and Mission Operations to improve product reliability and operational performance.

This position applies deep engineering expertise to identify fundamental technical failure mechanisms, validate corrective actions through engineering analysis and testing, and eliminate systemic product and process risks.

The Staff Quality Engineer operates across multiple manufacturing sites and product lines, working with cross functional teams on design opportunities, manufacturing processes, and operational readiness while establishing best practices for technical problem solving across the enterprise.




TECHNICAL PROBLEM SOLVING

 - Apply structured engineering methodologies to determine true physical, process, software, or systems root causes—not simply procedural gaps.

 - Utilize advanced analytical tools including Fault Tree Analysis, Fishbone, 5 Why, Statistical Analysis, Tolerance Stack Analysis, and FMEA.

 - Validate corrective actions using engineering data, experimentation, testing, and verification.

 - Drive permanent corrective actions that eliminate recurrence across products and manufacturing sites.




MULTI-SITE QUALITY LEADERSHIP

 - Provide technical quality leadership across multiple manufacturing locations.

 - Standardize RCCA methodologies and engineering investigations across the enterprise.

 - Coach site Quality Engineers on advanced engineering problem solving.

 - Lead enterprise technical reviews for recurring issues and customer escapes.

 - Support rapid problem escalation and recovery during production interruptions.




ROOT CAUSE & CORRECTIVE ACTION (RCCA)

 - Lead enterprise RCCA for manufacturing defects, supplier escapes, customer returns, field failures, and reliability issues.

 - Ensure investigations identify technical root causes rather than symptoms.




MANUFACTURING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

 - Improve manufacturing capability through engineering analysis.

 - Reduce defects through process optimization rather than increased inspection.

 - Support New Product Introduction (NPI) Quality activities across multiple product lines.




CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Program Management, Product Management, Mission Operations, and Executive Leadership.

 - Present technical findings and recommendations to cross functional teams.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering.

 - 10+ years of engineering aerospace, defense, automotive, or advanced manufacturing.

 - Demonstrated success solving complex engineering problems.

 - Extensive experience leading engineering-based RCCA.

 - Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations.

 - Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

 - Must be able to travel 30-50% of the time.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Design and development engineering management experience




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Establish an enterprise technical RCCA methodology across all manufacturing sites.

 - Reduce quality escapes through permanent corrective actions.

 - Improve manufacturing FPY.

 - Mentor Quality Engineers in advanced engineering problem solving.




BENEFITS

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

identity_held_roles.title: Director, Product Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 We are looking for a hands-on, high-impact Director, Product Quality  to lead our Field Quality and Failure Analysis engineering teams. In this role, you will hold ultimate accountability for overall field quality, reliability performance, and fleet health across all deployed commercial products. 

 You are a seasoned practitioner of rigorous problem-solving methodologies (8D, 5-Why, DMAIC) with a proven track record of diving deep into complex electromechanical, hardware, and firmware failures. You will bridge the gap between field service operations, customer sites, supplier quality, and internal product design teams to ensure field issues are contained rapidly, root-caused definitively, and prevented permanently. 

 About the Work 

 
 Own Field Quality & Fleet Health: Establish, monitor, and report on key field quality metrics (e.g., MTBI, MTTF, ARR, issue escape rates, service ticket turnaround time) for all shipping products and customer deployments. 

 Lead Failure Analysis (FA) & CAPA: Lead and grow a dedicated team of Failure Analysis Engineers. Drive rigorous Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes for field returns, hardware bugs, and system-level failures. 

 Field Containment & Rapid Response: Establish immediate containment protocols for critical field escalations, safety events, and unexpected fleet-wide failure trends to minimize customer downtime. 

 Cross-Functional Feedback Loop: Serve as the critical bridge between Field Operations, Customer Success, Hardware Engineering, Software/Firmware, and Supplier Quality. Drive design-for-reliability (DFR) feedback directly into next-generation product engineering. 

 Manage Closed-Loop Quality Systems: Implement and maintain robust Closed-Loop Corrective Action (CAPA) tracking across multi-site field deployments and repair depots. 

 Executive Communication & Governance: Host regular Field Quality Reviews with leadership, presenting objective data, failure Pareto analyses, root-cause findings, and measurable CAPA progress. 

 
 About You 

 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. 

 Experience: 10+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Field Quality, or Reliability Engineering within high-complexity hardware industries (Robotics, Automotive/EV, Aerospace, Autonomous Systems, or Complex Industrial Equipment). 

 Leadership: 5+ years of direct people management experience leading technical engineering teams (FA, Quality, or Sustaining Engineering). 

 Hands-on Expertise: Deep, practical experience executing physical failure analysis on electromechanical systems (actuators, harnesses, sensors, PCBAs, battery management systems, and precision mechanical linkages). 

 Methodologies: Certified or expert practitioner in structured root cause analysis tools (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Fault Tree Analysis, FMEA, Gauge R&R). 

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Advanced Degree: Master’s degree in Engineering Management or an Engineering discipline. 

 Certifications: Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE), or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. 

 Domain Experience: Experience managing field reliability for autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), humanoid robotics, or safety-critical industrial equipment. 

 Systems Exposure: Familiarity firmware diagnostic tools, and telemetry data analytics for remote fleet diagnostics. 

 
 Work Environment & Travel 

 
 Position is based out of our Salem, OR facility with regular access to testing labs, service centers, and assembly lines. 

 Occasional travel (up to 20%) to customer sites, field test locations, or primary suppliers may be required to investigate critical quality escapes. 

 
 
 Location 

 
 This is an onsite position at our Salem, OR office. 

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $162,000 — $210,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

identity_held_roles.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

 OUR MISSION 

 True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

 OUR VALUES 

 
 Be the offset.   We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

 What would it take?  We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

 It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

 
 BENEFITS & PERKS *

 
 Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

 Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

 Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees

 And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays

 Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

 
 *Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

 YOUR MISSION: 

 At True Anomaly, production is a strategic advantage. Our ability to rapidly build, integrate, test, and deliver high-performance systems at scale is critical to mission success and long-term competitiveness.

 As Vice President of Production, you will build our production organization into a high-rate, quality focused build and test machine.  You will drive vertical integration to achieve pace and cost targets while developing automation and test infrastructure to support lights out verification across multiple product lines and mission sets. You will own manufacturing, assembly/integration, EGSE design and production, quality, and test and test automation — building the operational systems, infrastructure, and teams required to scale efficiently without compromising quality or speed.

 This role is responsible for creating a data-driven production organization that continuously improves throughput, reliability, and cost while enabling rapid iteration and delivery across the business.

 Key Responsibilities 

 
 Lead all manufacturing, assembly, integration, and production test operations across the company’s product lines while supporting prototyping for research and development.

 Develop and execute the production strategy required to scale from development programs into repeatable, high-rate manufacturing.

 Own the operational execution of the company’s vertical integration efforts, including standing up internal manufacturing and test capabilities for propulsion systems, fluid systems, PCBAs, FlatSats, RF systems, and integrated space vehicles.

 Build scalable production systems, workflows, and operational infrastructure that improve throughput, quality, and delivery performance across complex hardware production environments.

 Drive implementation of lean manufacturing principles, automation, and data-driven operational management across production environments supporting spacecraft, missile defense, and mission-critical component and payload systems.

 Own development and deployment of production tooling, EGSE, fixtures, and automated test systems required to support scalable manufacturing, integration, and environmental test operations.

 Partner closely with Engineering teams to drive design-for-manufacturing and design-for-test principles into product development.

 Establish production metrics, dashboards, and operational review processes focused on cycle time, yield, labor efficiency, throughput, and cost reduction.

 Lead quality execution across manufacturing, integration, inspection, RF test, propulsion test, and production verification activities, ensuring quality is embedded into operational processes.

 Drive automation of test execution, production data collection, and operational reporting to improve repeatability, traceability, and decision-making.

 Collaborate with Supply Chain, Engineering, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness and execution across both classified and unclassified production environments.

 Build and mentor high-performing teams capable of supporting rapid company growth and operational scale.

 Support long-term facility, staffing, secure manufacturing, and production capacity planning to meet future mission demand.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or related technical field

 15+ years of experience leading manufacturing, production, integration, or operations organizations in complex technical industries

 Proven experience scaling production operations from development into repeatable manufacturing environments

 Strong background in manufacturing, assembly/integration, production test, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems

 Experience standing up vertically integrated manufacturing or test capabilities across areas such as propulsion systems, fluid systems, PCBAs, RF systems, or integrated vehicle production

 Demonstrated success driving operational excellence, quality improvement, and cost reduction initiatives

 Experience implementing data-driven manufacturing systems, KPIs, and production management processes

 Strong understanding of design-for-manufacturing, production scaling, environmental test, and test automation principles

 Experience operating within high-complexity manufacturing environments

 Proven ability to lead large multidisciplinary teams in fast-paced, highly technical environments

 Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Experience in aerospace, defense, launch vehicle, missile defense, or high-rate hardware manufacturing environments

 Familiarity with propulsion manufacturing and test operations, including additive manufacturing / 3D printing processes

 Experience with spacecraft integration and environmental test campaigns

 Familiarity with classified manufacturing and secure production operations

 Experience supporting rapid production scaling across multiple product lines

 Background implementing lean manufacturing or continuous improvement frameworks at scale

 Experience with automated manufacturing, MES, or production data systems

 Experience building operational organizations during periods of rapid company growth

 
 Compensation   

 
 Base Salary: $300,000 - $350,000 

 
 
 Equity + Benefits  including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO, and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave   

 
 Additional Requirements   

 
 Work Location – We observe an in-person work environment, and expect 4 days per week in office at the Company's Denver, CO headquarters or at our facility in Long Beach, California. 

 
 
 Security Clearance – Ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI clearance required. 

 
 This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. 

  
 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

 True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.

 To protect candidates and our company from application fraud and impersonation, we use third-party tools to verify applicant identity and detect fraudulent applications. Learn more in our Privacy Notice .

identity_held_roles.title: Head of Bedrock Operations Center
identity_held_roles.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Head of Bedrock Operations Center (BOC) to build and lead the central, always-on hub that oversees our deployed autonomous machines. As the Bedrock System deployments scale across new states, new machine types, and a next-generation platform, the BOC is how we keep every machine safe, productive, and supported around the clock.

This role owns three core functions: Remote Assistance, supporting autonomous machines in real time when they need a human decision; Customer & Partner Support, the single front door for customers, partners, and field teams; and Central Operations, which provides live visibility, dispatch coordination, and incident coordination and command.

The Head of BOC owns the Operations Center's operating model, organization, tooling requirements, performance, and manpower oversight. The BOC is accountable for the safe remote operations, uptime, and responsiveness our customers experience. Reporting to the VP of Operations, this leader is a critical thought partner to Product and to Operations Leads across the company.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operations Center Strategy & Build-out

 - Define the BOC operating model, org structure, and coverage model (shifts, time zones, follow-the-sun) as the fleet scales

 - Build and lead the BOC leadership team and a growing workforce of shift leads and specialists

 - Own workforce planning and ensure adequate, qualified staffing; Partner with Product and Engineering on machines-per-operator ratios against fleet growth, product mix, and new machine types

 - Own the physical and technical readiness of the Operations Center, including infrastructure, redundancy, connectivity, and business continuity

Remote Assistance

 - Own round-the-clock remote operations for autonomous machines, including response-time SLAs, escalation protocols, and clear decision authority

 - Establish safety-first standards for remote interventions, remote stops, and hand-offs to on-site personnel, in partnership with Safety teams

 - Build training, certification, and quality-assurance programs for remote assistance operators

 - Analyze intervention data and partner with Autonomy Engineering to reduce interventions and improve machine autonomy over time

Customer & Partner Support

 - Build and lead a tiered support function (L1 / L2 / L3) with clear escalation paths into Field Operations, Service, Hardware, RA, and/ or Engineering

 - Define and deliver support SLAs tailored to each product line and customer commitment

 - Own ticketing, knowledge base, and customer communication standards; turn voice-of-customer trends into fixes

 - Partner with the Commercial team on customer onboarding, service commitments, and account health

Central Operations / Command & Control

 - Own live, fleet-wide situational awareness: machine status, health, location, and utilization across every site

 - Coordinate daily dispatch, service, and maintenance with Field Operations, including parts and technician routing

 - Serve as incident command for operational and safety events, with clear playbooks for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident review

 - Own runbooks, shift hand-off standards, and change management for new sites, new machine types, and new platforms

Performance & Analytics

 - Define and track core BOC metrics: intervention rate and response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, fleet uptime, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to leadership

 - Lead continuous improvement through process, automation, and data, increasing the number of machines each operator can safely support


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Autonomous machines get fast, safe human support whenever they need it

 - Customers and partners have one clear front door and consistently fast resolution

 - Real-time visibility into every machine and site, with incidents handled calmly and transparently

 - Machines-per-operator rises steadily as intervention insights drive autonomy improvements

 - The Operations Center scales ahead of fleet growth, new sites, and new machine types without a drop in service


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - 12+ years in operations leadership, including 5+ years building and leading 24/7 or mission-critical operations (command centers, remote operations, network or fleet operations, or large-scale support organizations)

 - Experience building an operations organization from early stage to scale, including hiring and developing managers and shift leads and managing large hourly and/or contract workforces

 - Track record defining and managing SLAs, escalation paths, and incident response in safety-critical or high-availability environments

 - Experience influencing engineering, product, and commercial leaders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable with operational data, dashboards, and forecasting models (SQL / BI tools a plus)

 - Experience with workforce planning, scheduling, and shift-based operations

 - Excellent written and verbal communication with customers, field crews, and executives

Preferred

 - Experience running operations centers for autonomous vehicles, robotics, trucking, aviation, or mining

 - Experience leading remote assistance, teleoperation, or fleet response teams for autonomous systems

 - Familiarity with heavy machinery and/or the construction industry

 - Experience building B2B or technical support for industrial equipment or hardware products

 - Familiarity with fleet telemetry, monitoring and alerting, ticketing, and workforce-management tools

 - Experience launching operations across multiple regions or time zones

 - Continuous improvement / Lean / Six Sigma experience


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Every autonomous machine Bedrock deploys depends on the Operations Center to keep it safe, productive, and supported. You'll build the function that lets our fleet scale with confidence, and directly shape the experience every customer and partner has with Bedrock.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
identity_held_roles.description:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

 


THE ROLE

We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.

This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.

 - Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.

 - Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.

 - Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.

 - Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.

 - Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.

 - Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.

 - Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.

 - Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.

 - Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.

 - You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.

 - Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.

 - You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.

 - You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.

 - You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.

 - 8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.

 - Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.

 


WORKING CONDITIONS

Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.

 


WHY THIS ROLE

You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.

 


HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

 - Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

 - Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

 - Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

 - Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

 - Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

 - Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

 - A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft.

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Supply Chain (Robot Production)
identity_held_roles.description:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

Every part that goes into our robot: who makes it, at what price, on what lead time, to what quality. This is the hands-on role. You build the supplier base for production, develop domestic sources for the sub-systems that need them, and make sure the line never waits on a part. You start with a bill of materials, a design team and a few suppliers; you end with a qualified, dual-sourced supply chain that supports production with our manufacturing partner. You are at our facility, at the partner and at suppliers more than you are at a desk.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Be on the floor: at our facility, at our manufacturing partner and at suppliers; first articles, line-down calls and recoveries are yours.

 - Build the supplier base: source, qualify and manage suppliers for machined and cast structures, gears and actuators, motors, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two sources for every critical sub-system.

 - Develop domestic suppliers for the sub-systems that need them, and keep the content records that come with selling into regulated markets.

 - Run the commercial work day to day: RFQs, should-cost, piece price and tooling negotiation, payment and warranty terms; work with Legal on supplier agreements.

 - Sit in design reviews from the start: flag long-lead, single-source and high-risk parts before design freeze; bring supplier capability into the design.

 - Own clear-to-build and the plan: every unit on the schedule has a complete kit before it starts; a rolling plan the line, the partner and the suppliers all see; capacity planning with suppliers ahead of demand; inventory accuracy and safety stock by part class.

 - Own the BOM in production: cost roll-ups by phase, engineering change control with the design team and Manufacturing Engineering, cost-down from pilot to volume.

 - Build the supplier quality loop with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality: first article and PPAP where it applies, incoming inspection, supplier scorecards and quarterly reviews, corrective action and recovery.

 - Run logistics: inbound, between our facility and our partner's, import and export paperwork with Legal, spares and service parts.

 - Run the systems we have and help stand up the next ones: part numbering, BOM control, MRP; own the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, PPV, inventory).




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - You have built a supplier base for a hardware product going into production, not managed or handed to you, and you produce results in weeks, not quarters.

 - Deep experience with machined and cast metal parts, gears or actuators, motors, PCBAs and harnesses, and the suppliers who make them; you read drawings and GD&T.

 - You have developed new suppliers in new regions and qualified them to a standard.

 - Strong commercial record: you have negotiated price, tooling and terms with suppliers and contract manufacturers.

 - You are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and cost roll-ups, and comfortable with the people who design the product.

 - 8 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or supplier development for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what the systems look like at scale; you have led a small team or are ready to; engineering degree preferred.

 - Bonus: robotics or automotive; contract manufacturer selection and transition; import and export compliance; APICS or CPSM.




WORKING CONDITIONS

Office and production environments; travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 30%.




HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

 - Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

 - Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

 - Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

 - Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

 - Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

 - Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

 - A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

You own the supply chain for a general-purpose robot going from prototype to production: every part in the bill of materials, from actuators, gears and motors to structures, PCBAs, harnesses, batteries and sensors, and every supplier and manufacturing partner behind them. You build it from the ground up, in the United States and abroad, and you build the team that runs it. The scale goes from tens of units to hundreds to thousands, and the supply base, partners and processes that got us to today will not be the ones that get us there. Building the next version is the job.

This is a role for someone who has done it before, in the trenches, and wants to do it again with a product that matters more than the last one. You will spend your weeks with suppliers, on the floor with our manufacturing partners, in design reviews with the engineers who are still changing the parts, and with the leadership team on the decisions that shape the company. Strategy and execution are the same job here.




WHY THIS ROLE

Few people get to decide how a new category of machine gets built. Eno is dexterous, wheeled and already working with real customers, built today with a supply base and partners that got us here. The next version of that supply chain, the one that takes us to volume, is yours to shape: what we make and what we buy, where in the world it comes from, which partners we grow with, and what the robot costs at scale. Those choices will be visible in every unit we ship for years.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Strategy. Set the supply chain strategy from pilot to volume: make versus buy, regional footprint, domestic content for regulated markets, single versus dual source by sub-system, and the order in which each piece moves as volume grows.

Partners. Own contract manufacturer and partner relationships at the executive level: selection, agreements, capacity commitments, cost and quality performance, and the transfer of sub-assemblies between regions and partners when the plan calls for it.

Cost. Own the cost roadmap: should-cost and total-cost models, the path from pilot cost to target cost, tooling and capital decisions, long-term agreements with pricing that steps down with volume; partner with Finance on working capital and with Legal on supplier agreements.

Supply base. Build the supplier base for the hard sub-systems: actuators, gears and motors, machined and cast structures, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two qualified sources for every critical part, in the regions the product and our customers require.

Risk. Run capacity and risk: capacity ahead of demand, lead-time and allocation strategy for constrained parts, tariff and trade exposure, geopolitical and single-point-of-failure risk, and a plan for each.

Team. Build and lead the organization: sourcing, supplier development, planning, supplier quality and logistics. Hire the leaders under you, hold a high bar, set the operating cadence and the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, purchase price variance, inventory, supplier quality) and the readout to the leadership team and the board.

Systems. Stand up what a scaled organization runs on, with Manufacturing Engineering and Platform: part numbering, BOM and change control, MRP and ERP, supplier portal, traceability. Lightweight first, then more.

Design. Be in the design conversation from the start: bring supplier capability and cost into the product early, and push the design toward what can be built at volume at the right price.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Built it before. You have led the supply chain organization for a complex electromechanical product from first builds through production at scale, and either built the supply base from scratch or moved it to a new geography. Robotics, electric vehicles, aerospace, consumer electronics or medical devices.

Leader of leaders. You have built a supply chain organization, hired its managers, and run it on numbers; you can still do the work yourself when the team is three people.

Commercial weight. You have negotiated with contract manufacturers and tier-one suppliers at the executive level and closed long-term agreements that held up under pressure.

Global. You have sourced across regions, including Asia and North America, and moved production between them.

Cost record. You can walk through a BOM cost-down from pilot to volume part by part, and you know where the money hides.

Technical. You read drawings and GD&T, you understand actuators, gearboxes, motors and PCBAs well enough to challenge an engineer constructively, and you are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and MRP.

Pace. You default to urgency, operate without a playbook, and are comfortable before the systems exist.

Experience. Typically 10 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or manufacturing operations for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and time in a company that was building it. Engineering degree preferred.




WHAT ELSE YOU NEED TO KNOW

On-site in the Bay Area. Travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 40%.




HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.
